quotes.quote: Exome analyses revealed a significantly higher number of single nucleotide variants (SNVs) in HP‐exposed DGCs than in HP‐naïve DGCs (HP‐exposed DGCs; 1.97 [0.48 minimum–7.19 maximum] and HP‐naïve DGCs; 1.09 [0.38–3.68] per megabase, p = 0.0003).

The data generated in this study have been submitted to the National Bioscience Database Center (NBDC; https://biosciencedbc.jp/en/ ) and NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/ ) under accession numbers hum0338 (exome BAM files [raw data] are available through controlled‐access of NBDC) and GSE129219 (RNA‐seq TPM file; the raw data will not be available through controlled‐access resources such as dbGaP or EGA).

G1.rationale: The principal result is a statistical comparison of SNV burden computed from exome sequencing data; the deposit lists RNA-seq TPM file GSE129219, but exome raw data are controlled-access, so a third party cannot fully re-run the exome computation from the listed files alone.

G2.rationale: The first quantitative result in the Results section is the SNV burden comparison, with a named primary numerical endpoint (SNVs per megabase) and p-value.

G3.rationale: The listed deposit GSE129219 contains RNA-seq TPM data, which are not the inputs for the exome-based SNV burden target; the exome BAM files are under controlled access at NBDC and not in the listing.

G4.rationale: The main text defers detailed exome variant-calling and SNV burden computation methods to supplementary materials, which are not included in the provided segments, so implementability without original code is uncertain.
